propositions.text: The claimant is a citizen of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines claiming refugee protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1).
propositions.quote: The claimant, XXXXX XXXXX, is a citizen of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines. He is claiming refugee protection under section 96 and subsection 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).

paragraphs.summary: The claimant is a citizen of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines claiming refugee protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1), court states.

propositions.text: The claimant's designated representative is XXXXX XXXXX from XXXXX.
propositions.quote: XXXXX XXXXX, from XXXXX, acted as the claimant's designated representative.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant's designated representative is XXXXX XXXXX from XXXXX, court states.

propositions.text: The claimant was persecuted for criticizing authorities and practising Rastafarianism and had mental health difficulties.
propositions.quote: The claimant, who was a XXXXX and who apparently XXXXX XXXXX in Saint Vincent, experienced various acts of persecution because he criticized the authorities in place and because he practised Rastafarianism. The claimant also had difficulties stemming from his mental health problems.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges persecution for criticizing authorities and practising Rastafarianism and has mental health difficulties, applicant says.

propositions.text: The claimant arrived in Canada in 2008, consulted his lawyer, filed a refugee claim, but did not complete or submit his PIF.
propositions.quote: The claimant arrived in Canada in XXXXX 2008. He consulted his lawyer, wrote up his story and filed his refugee protection claim. On October 28, 2008, his claim was referred to the Refugee Protection Division (RPD); however, the claimant did not contact his lawyer, and his Personal Information Form (PIF) was never completed and submitted.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant arrived in Canada in 2008, filed a refugee claim but did not complete or submit his PIF, court states.

propositions.text: On January 30, 2009, the RPD found the claimant abandoned his claim.
propositions.quote: On January 30, 2009, the RPD concluded that the claimant had abandoned his claim.

propositions.text: On April 21, 2010, an application to reopen was allowed due to claimant's mental health and hospitalization on hearing day.
propositions.quote: On April 21, 2010, an application to reopen was allowed because of the claimant's mental health problems and because of allegations that he had been hospitalized on the day of the hearing on the abandonment of his claim.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the claim abandoned in 2009 but allowed reopening in 2010 due to mental health and hospitalization, earlier decision-maker found.

propositions.text: The panel determines the claimant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection after analyzing evidence.
propositions.quote: After analyzing all of the evidence, the panel determines that the claimant is not a "Convention refugee" or a "person in need of protection."

paragraphs.summary: The panel determines the claimant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection, court concludes.

propositions.text: The panel is satisfied with the claimant's identity based on passport and name change certificate.
propositions.quote: The panel is satisfied as to the claimant's identity, which was demonstrated by the presence in the file of a copy of his passport, in the name of XXXXX XXXXX,1 and a certificate of a change of name from XXXXX XXXXX to XXXXX XXXXX.2

paragraphs.summary: The panel is satisfied with the claimant's identity based on passport and name change certificate, court finds.

propositions.text: The claimant allegedly has mental health problems but refuses treatment and psychiatric assessment.
propositions.quote: The claimant allegedly suffers from some mental health problems. There is no official diagnosis for the problems, because he refuses to undergo treatment for them. The claimant, who is in detention at the Immigration Prevention Centre, was to consult a physician, in October 2010, for a psychiatric assessment; however, the claimant refused to undergo such an assessment.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant allegedly has mental health problems but refuses treatment and psychiatric assessment, court states.

propositions.text: The claimant's statements were often incoherent and his behaviour erratic, noted by lawyer, representative, sister, and panel.
propositions.quote: The claimant's lawyer, some people who worked with him during his detention at the Immigration Prevention Centre,3 his designated representative, his sister, who testified at the hearing, and the panel before whom he testified, all noted that his statements were often incoherent. The claimant's designated representative described his behaviour as [translation] "erratic," which is consistent with what the panel observed in the hearing room. The claimant's lawyer also indicated the he had difficulty cooperating with her.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant's statements were incoherent and behaviour erratic, noted by lawyer, representative, sister, and panel, earlier decision-maker finds.

propositions.text: The claimant cannot fully appreciate proceedings; a representative was designated and procedural accommodations were made.
propositions.quote: The panel is of the opinion that the claimant is unable to fully appreciate the nature of the proceedings, which is why a representative was designated for him under subsection 167(2) of the IRPA. Although no application was filed to have the claimant declared a vulnerable person, the panel ensured that, during the hearing, the necessary procedural accommodations were made to make it easier for the claimant to testify and present the elements in support of his claim.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant cannot fully appreciate proceedings; a representative was designated and accommodations made, court finds.

propositions.text: The claimant was invited to speak but allowed to avoid being present during sister's testimony and lawyer's statements.
propositions.quote: For example, the claimant was invited to speak about his claim, but the panel respected his wish to not be in the room during his sister's testimony and during his lawyer's statements.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant was invited to speak but allowed to avoid being present during sister's testimony and lawyer's statements, court states.

propositions.text: The panel allowed the lawyer to ask questions first and the representative to intervene; panel and officer clarified points due to claimant's defiance.
propositions.quote: The panel also allowed the claimant's lawyer to ask the questions first and allowed his designated representative to intervene when he thought it appropriate. Because of the claimant's defiance toward his lawyer, the tribunal officer and the panel both tried, in turn, to clarify certain points.

paragraphs.summary: The panel allowed lawyer and representative to question; clarified points due to claimant's defiance, court states.

propositions.text: The panel scheduled a post-hearing meeting to file additional documents found by claimant's sister and allowed documentary evidence on Rastafarians and mental illness.
propositions.quote: In addition, the panel scheduled a meeting after the hearing to find out about the XXXXX that the claimant had apparently XXXXX and that could not be filed at the hearing. During that meeting, which took place five days after the hearing, the claimant's lawyer informed the panel that the claimant's sister had found some supplementary documents in a suitcase he had left at her home. The panel allowed those documents to be filed, on the grounds of their relevance.5 The panel also granted an additional delay so that some documentary evidence could be filed on the situation of Rastafarians in the Caribbean and on the treatment of people with mental illness.

paragraphs.summary: The panel scheduled a post-hearing meeting to file additional documents and allowed evidence on Rastafarians and mental illness, court states.

propositions.text: The claimant alleges persecution for his controversial opinions and conversion to Rastafarianism, worsening his mental health.
propositions.quote: Basically, it is alleged that the claimant was a XXXXX in his country and that he was persecuted by the authorities for his controversial opinions, which he allegedly expressed about the government. Also, the claimant converted to Rastafarianism, which apparently prompted him, in 1995, to change his name to one that more clearly expressed his faith and which allegedly became a new reason for his persecution. That alleged persecution supposedly had a negative effect on the claimant's mental health, which only served to aggravate his already difficult situation.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges persecution for controversial opinions and Rastafarianism conversion, worsening mental health, applicant says.

propositions.text: The claimant alleges job loss, eviction, government harassment, assault, passport revocation, poisoning, theft, failed business, and attempted murder.
propositions.quote: The claimant described his difficulties, at question 31 of his PIF. He stated that he was fired from his job in 1992, was evicted from several apartments, had trouble finding other jobs, XXXXX that the Saint Vincent government allegedly XXXXX XXXXX and was beaten up by some people who supported the government in 1996. In addition, the claimant's passport was allegedly revoked. He also claimed to have been poisoned every year until 2003. He also claimed that XXXXX XXXXX and XXXXX XXXXX had been stolen and that he had tried to start up a XXXXX XXXXX, but that initiative failed in 2002, when three of the investors apparently pulled out. On a number of occasions, people allegedly tried to discredit the claimant's work, the police supposedly dropped their investigation into the XXXXX theft and the claimant allegedly managed to obtain a passport after surviving an attempted murder that allegedly forced him to live on the street.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges job loss, eviction, government harassment, assault, passport revocation, poisoning, theft, failed business, and attempted murder, applicant says.

propositions.text: At hearing, claimant said prior claims were no longer valid and accepted deportation, fearing no harm on return.
propositions.quote: At the hearing, the claimant stated that what he had declared in his refugee protection claim was no longer valid. He stated that he agreed with the fact that he was going to be deported. He reiterated that what he feared two years earlier no longer existed and that what he had criticized the government for was [translation] "ancient history." When questioned again about what he had gone through in Saint Vincent, the claimant stated that it had happened in 2008, that it was a long time ago, and that he no longer wanted to obtain refugee status. When asked, [translation] "What would happen to you if you had to return to Saint Vincent?", the claimant replied that nothing in particular would happen to him. He stated that he would not have any problems if he had to return and that the truth must XXXXX XXXXX.

paragraphs.summary: At hearing, claimant said prior claims were invalid, accepted deportation, and feared no harm on return, court states.

propositions.text: Claimant's lawyer and representative alleged claimant misunderstood hearing purpose and minimized risks to gain release from detention.
propositions.quote: Since the claimant had nothing else to add, the panel let him leave the room. His lawyer and his designated representative then alleged that the claimant did not really understand the purpose of the proceedings and that he may have confused his refugee protection hearing with a detention review hearing. Since the claimant's main focus is on getting out of detention, he might have minimized what would happen to him in the hope of being released.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant's lawyer and representative alleged claimant misunderstood hearing and minimized risks to gain release, court states.

propositions.text: The panel suggested the representative explain hearing purpose to claimant; claimant declined to add further evidence.
propositions.quote: Given that information, the panel suggested that the designated representative meet privately with the claimant to explain to him once again the purpose of this hearing, and that the claimant could return and speak to the panel if he felt it necessary. The designated representative returned to the hearing room and reported that the claimant had stated that he had nothing to add.

paragraphs.summary: The panel suggested the representative explain hearing purpose to claimant; claimant declined to add further evidence, court states.

propositions.text: Claimant's sister testified about claimant's education, work, and her limited knowledge of his illness.
propositions.quote: The claimant's sister, XXXXX XXXXX, testified. She stated that her older brother had been a father figure to her. She stated that she has always had tremendous admiration for her brother, an erudite man who had worked hard to get an education, who had been a XXXXX and who had worked for the XXXXX XXXXX. The claimant's sister stated that she had left Saint Vincent in 1997 and that she did not know the claimant when he was sick. She apparently went back to Saint Vincent to visit in 2000, but allegedly did not see her brother then.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant's sister testified about his education, work, and limited knowledge of his illness, witness states.

propositions.text: The sister received family calls about claimant's problems including job loss, theft, beatings, and acid attack leading to hospitalization.
propositions.quote: The claimant's sister allegedly received some calls from the family informing her that her brother was having problems. She was apparently told that her brother had been fired from his XXXXX when he expressed his beliefs in Rastafarianism, that some XXXXX and XXXXX had been stolen from him, that he had been beaten up often, and that acid had been thrown in his face, which led to his being hospitalized.

paragraphs.summary: The sister received family calls about claimant's problems including job loss, theft, beatings, and acid attack, witness states.

propositions.text: Ms. XXXXX knew in 2008 her older brother had mental health problems and a cousin contacted her about his condition.
propositions.quote: Ms. XXXXX apparently knew in 2008 that her older brother was suffering from mental health problems. A cousin who was working at a XXXXX where the claimant was staying allegedly contacted her to tell her that he was not well.

propositions.text: Some family members asked Ms. XXXXX to arrange to get her brother out of the country.
propositions.quote: Some family members allegedly asked Ms. XXXXX to arrange to get him out of the country.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds Ms. XXXXX knew in 2008 about her brother's mental health issues and family asked her to help get him out of the country.

propositions.text: Ms. XXXXX had information that her brother was on medication in Saint Vincent but likely stopped it in Canada, worsening his condition.
propositions.quote: According to the information that Ms. XXXXX had, her brother had been on medication when he was living in Saint Vincent. When he arrived in Canada, the effect of the medication, which he most likely stopped taking, gradually diminished and his condition seemed to worsen.

paragraphs.summary: The panel notes Ms. XXXXX's information that her brother stopped medication after arriving in Canada, worsening his condition.

propositions.text: Ms. XXXXX believed her brother was persecuted for criticizing the government and ostracized for being Rastafarian.
propositions.quote: Ms. XXXXX stated that she believed that her brother had been persecuted for criticizing the government and that he had been ostracized for being Rastafarian.

propositions.text: She stated there is discrimination against Rastafarians in Saint Vincent, including difficulty getting jobs and police cutting hair if institutionalized.
propositions.quote: She stated that there is a great deal of discrimination against Rastafarians in Saint Vincent, that it is difficult for someone who wears a typically Rastafarian hairstyle to get a job and that it is quite possible that the police would cut her brother's hair if he were to be institutionalized again.

propositions.text: She stated the claimant risked being beaten again if returned and that his mental health problems stemmed from abuse.
propositions.quote: She stated that the claimant risked being beaten again if he returned to his country and that she thought that his mental health problems stemmed from abuse he has suffered.

paragraphs.summary: Ms. XXXXX believes her brother was persecuted for political and religious reasons and faces discrimination and risk of abuse if returned.

propositions.text: The panel understands mental illness difficulties but cannot conclude a serious possibility of persecution if claimant returns to Saint Vincent.
propositions.quote: the panel cannot, on the basis of the evidence at its disposal, conclude that there is a serious possibility that the claimant would be persecuted if he had to return to Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds no serious possibility of persecution upon claimant's return despite understanding mental illness challenges.

propositions.text: The panel believes claimant was a XXXXX in Saint Vincent and has documents corroborating this.
propositions.quote: The panel is willing to believe that the claimant is telling the truth when he states that he was a XXXXX in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines. He has documents corroborating his claims in that regard.

propositions.text: The panel believes claimant is Rastafarian and has XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX, part of his faith.
propositions.quote: The panel also believes that the claimant is Rastafarian and that he has XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX, an intrinsic component of his faith.

propositions.text: The panel gives claimant benefit of doubt that he made critical comments about Saint Vincent authorities and establishment.
propositions.quote: The panel is even prepared to give the claimant the benefit of the doubt that he XXXXX XXXXX that were critical of the Saint Vincent authorities and of the "establishment."

paragraphs.summary: The panel believes claimant's status as XXXXX, Rastafarian faith, and critical comments about authorities.

propositions.text: The panel lacks enough evidence to conclude claimant was persecuted in Saint Vincent.
propositions.quote: the panel does not have enough evidence to conclude that the claimant was a victim of persecution when he was living in Saint Vincent.

propositions.text: Evidence includes vague claimant statements, a likely mentally ill person denying problems, and sister not present in Saint Vincent.
propositions.quote: the panel has only vague information from the claimant's statements at question 31 of his PIF, who is likely mentally ill and who denied having problems at the hearing, and from his sister, who was not in Saint Vincent when these events allegedly occurred and who apparently obtained this information from another family member, without providing more details.

propositions.text: The panel does not know who attacked claimant, circumstances, or cause of attacks.
propositions.quote: The panel does not know who allegedly attacked the claimant, what the circumstances were surrounding the alleged attacks and what the apparent cause of it was.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds insufficient evidence about claimant's persecution, attacks, or circumstances in Saint Vincent.

propositions.text: Documentary evidence shows Saint Vincent is a parliamentary democracy with freedom of expression and XXXXX XXXXX.
propositions.quote: According to the documentary evidence, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines is a parliamentary democracy where there is freedom of expression and XXXXX XXXXX.

propositions.text: Government generally respects these rights in practice.
propositions.quote: The documentary evidence also indicates that the government generally respects these rights in practice.

propositions.text: Quote: "XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX."
propositions.quote: "XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX."

paragraphs.summary: Documentary evidence shows Saint Vincent is a democracy respecting freedom of expression and XXXXX XXXXX.

propositions.text: 1993 document reports Rastafarians sometimes face police and judicial discrimination, illegal searches, violence, and job difficulties.
propositions.quote: With regard to the fact that the claimant is Rastafarian, according to a document from 1993, people who practise Rastafarianism do sometimes face discrimination by the police and by the judicial system. For example, the police apparently perform illegal searches of Rastafarians and use violence against them during interrogations or detentions. It is also reportedly difficult for Rastafarians to find a job.

paragraphs.summary: A 1993 document reports Rastafarians face police and judicial discrimination and job difficulties.

propositions.text: A 2004 interview found no complaints of discrimination in housing, education, or employment but some police harassment for marijuana use.
propositions.quote: Another, more recent, source, however, reported as follows: "With regard to discrimination faced by Rastafarians, the coordinator of the Saint Vincent and the Grenadines Human Rights Association (SVGHRA) based in Kingstown stated in a 28 October 2004 telephone interview that her organization had not received any complaints from Rastafarians who faced discrimination in connection with housing, education or employment. However, the coordinator did mention that she was aware of some harassment of Rastafarians by the police for marijuana use and cultivation, which, considering the country's laws, "would be expected10."

paragraphs.summary: A 2004 source reports no discrimination complaints except police harassment for marijuana use among Rastafarians.

propositions.text: A third source reports Rastafarians complain government prohibits marijuana use integral to their rituals.
propositions.quote: Similar information appears in a third documentary source: "Rastafarians complained that the government prohibited the use of marijuana, which they claimed was integral to their religious rituals11."

paragraphs.summary: A third source reports Rastafarians complain about marijuana prohibition affecting their religious rituals.

propositions.text: UNHCR Handbook states not all discrimination is persecution; persecution involves serious prejudicial consequences.
propositions.quote: The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees' Handbook on Procedures and Criteria for Determining Refugee Status states that not all discrimination is necessarily persecution: "(c) Discrimination 54. Differences in the treatment of various groups do indeed exist to a greater or lesser extent in many societies. Persons who receive less favourable treatment as a result of such differences are not necessarily victims of persecution. It is only in certain circumstances that discrimination will amount to persecution. This would be so if measures of discrimination lead to consequences of a substantially prejudicial nature for the person concerned, e.g. serious restrictions on his right to earn his livelihood, his right to practise his religion, or his access to normally available educational facilities. 55. Where measures of discrimination are, in themselves, not of a serious character, they may nevertheless give rise to a reasonable fear of persecution if they produce, in the mind of the person concerned, a feeling of apprehension and insecurity as regards his future existence. Whether or not such measures of discrimination in themselves amount to persecution must be determined in the light of all the circumstances. A claim to fear of persecution will of course be stronger where a person has been the victim of a number of discriminatory measures of this type and where there is thus a cumulative element involved."

paragraphs.summary: UNHCR Handbook explains discrimination is not always persecution; persecution requires serious prejudicial consequences.

propositions.text: Panel cannot conclude serious possibility of persecution for critical comments or Rastafarian religion due to lack of evidence.
propositions.quote: the panel cannot conclude that there is a serious possibility that the claimant will be persecuted for making comments critical of the government or the "establishment," or because he was Rastafarian.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds no serious possibility of persecution for claimant's political comments or religion due to insufficient evidence.

propositions.text: Panel cannot conclude mental health problems alone or combined with religion justify refugee protection.
propositions.quote: the panel cannot conclude that, in and of themselves, or combined with the claimant's religion, they constitute grounds for granting him refugee protection.

propositions.text: Documentary evidence shows some prejudice and taboos about mental illness in the Caribbean but no persecution.
propositions.quote: The documentary evidence filed by the claimant's lawyer indicates that there is some prejudice with regard to mental illness in the Caribbean and that some taboos remain, but nothing indicates that people with mental illness are persecuted.

propositions.text: Quote: "Too often, and especially in the Caribbean, ... we tend to view people with mental health illnesses as taboo..."
propositions.quote: "Too often, and especially in the Caribbean, ... we tend to view people with mental health illnesses as taboo, rather than recognizing that with treatment, recovery is possible. We also tend to forget that mental illness is not the result of personal weakness, but it can affect persons of any age, race, religion or income12."

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds mental illness alone or with religion does not justify protection; evidence shows prejudice but no persecution.

propositions.text: Panel knows claimant received care and medication in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.
propositions.quote: from the little the panel knows, the claimant received care and medication to improve his condition when he was in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.

paragraphs.summary: The panel notes claimant received care and medication in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.

propositions.text: Panel finds claimant is not a person in need of protection under IRPA subsection 97(1).
propositions.quote: the panel is of the opinion that the claimant is also not a "person in need of protection" under subsection 97(1) of the IRPA, since he did not demonstrate that he would be subjected to a risk to his life or to a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment that do not result from his country's inability to provide proper medical or health care.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds claimant is not a person in need of protection under IRPA subsection 97(1).

propositions.text: Claimant did not prove serious possibility of persecution on Convention grounds or risk of torture, death, or cruel treatment if returned.
propositions.quote: the panel concludes that the claimant did not discharge the burden of establishing that there is a serious possibility that he was persecuted on one of the Convention grounds. He did not establish that, on a balance of probabilities, if he were to return to Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, he would be personally subjected to a danger of torture or to a risk to his life or to a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment.

paragraphs.summary: The panel concludes claimant failed to prove serious possibility of persecution or risk of torture, death, or cruel treatment if returned.

propositions.text: Panel determines claimant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.
propositions.quote: the panel determines that the claimant is not a "Convention refugee" or a "person in need of protection."

paragraphs.summary: The panel determines claimant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.

propositions.text: Panel rejects refugee protection claim of XXXXX.
propositions.quote: The panel rejects the refugee protection claim of XXXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The panel rejects the refugee protection claim of XXXXX.
